title: Should I Join?
learning_objectives: Use a decision matrix to evaluate options
Weigh pros and cons of activities

events.description: Three clubs are recruiting! Drama Club (3hr/week, performances, social), Coding Club (2hr/week, build projects, smaller group), and Soccer Team (5hr/week, competitive, large team). You have 10 hours/week of free time. How do you start deciding?

choices.label: Try all three for a week each
choices.effect: Hands-on research! After trying each, you have real data for your decision.

choices.label: Rate each club on fun, learning, time, social
choices.effect: A decision matrix! You score each option and compare. Structured thinking!

choices.label: Talk to kids in each club about their experience
choices.effect: First-hand accounts! Their experiences help you imagine yourself in each club.

events.description: You're leaning toward two clubs. Drama is super fun but 3 hours during your busiest day. Coding is flexible timing and you love building things. Can you do both?

choices.label: Join both — 5 hours total fits!
choices.effect: 5 of your 10 free hours — totally doable! And the skills are so different.

choices.label: Just coding — keep more free time
choices.effect: One focused commitment leaves time for other things. Quality over quantity!

choices.label: Ask if Drama has a less intensive role
choices.effect: The director says you can help with set design — only 1.5 hours! Now both fit perfectly!

events.description: A month in, your best friend joins Soccer Team and wants you to switch. You're happy in your current clubs but feel pulled. How do you think through it?

choices.label: Go back to your decision criteria
choices.effect: Your criteria haven't changed! Soccer doesn't score higher just because a friend joined.

choices.label: Add 'being with best friend' as a new factor
choices.effect: Social connection is valid! You recalculate and decide based on the updated matrix.

choices.label: Stick with your plan — see your friend other times
choices.effect: You can be friends without being in the same club! Independence is a strength.

events.description: End of semester reflection: how do you feel about your club decision?

choices.label: It was the right choice for me!
choices.effect: Trusting your decision-making process paid off! You chose based on what matters to YOU.

choices.label: I'd choose differently next time — and that's okay
choices.effect: Learning what you like and don't like IS the value of trying! Great self-awareness.

choices.label: I want to try something new next semester
choices.effect: Growth mindset! You can always explore new activities. The decision skills you built carry over.

recap_template: You used structured decision-making to choose activities! Whether you use a matrix, talk to people, or try things out, having a process leads to better choices.
positive_framing_rules: Never say the student made the wrong choice of club
Frame changing your mind as growth, not indecision
Celebrate the decision process over the specific outcome
ai_variation_allowed: Change the specific clubs or activities

title: Group Project Planner

events.description: Your team has a history presentation due in 10 days. Tasks: research (4 hours), write the script (3 hours), create slides (3 hours), and practice presenting (2 hours). Mia loves research, Leo is great at design, Sam is a good speaker. How do you divide the work?

choices.label: Play to strengths: Mia researches, Leo designs, you and Sam write + present
choices.effect: Everyone does what they're best at! The project will shine because of diverse talents.

choices.label: Everyone does a bit of everything
choices.effect: Equal exposure! Everyone learns each skill, even if it takes a bit longer.

choices.label: Work in pairs: Mia+you on content, Leo+Sam on design+presentation
choices.effect: Pair work means built-in support! Nobody works alone.

events.description: Day 5 check-in. Mia's research is excellent and Leo's slides look great. But Sam hasn't started their part yet. How do you handle it?

choices.label: Check in — 'Hey Sam, how's it going? Need help?'
choices.effect: Sam was overwhelmed by other homework. Once you understood, you adjusted the plan. Empathy + problem-solving!

choices.label: Split Sam's part among the team
choices.effect: Everyone takes a small piece. The work gets done and Sam catches up when they can.

choices.label: Create mini-deadlines so nothing falls behind again
choices.effect: Mini check-ins every 2 days! The team stays on track without anyone feeling singled out.

events.description: Day 8. During practice, Mia and Leo disagree about how to present a section. Mia wants lots of facts, Leo wants more visuals. The argument is getting tense.

choices.label: Find a middle ground — facts WITH visuals
choices.effect: An infographic! Mia's facts presented in Leo's visual style. Both feel heard and it's better than either idea alone!

choices.label: Ask 'What would the audience prefer?'
choices.effect: Shifting focus to the audience dissolves the personal disagreement. Data + visuals for the win!

choices.label: Try both approaches and see which works better
choices.effect: Testing removes opinion from the equation! The team picks what actually works best.

events.description: Presentation day! How does the team feel?

choices.label: Proud of what we built together
choices.effect: The presentation is a hit! Working through challenges made the team stronger.

choices.label: We learned as much about teamwork as history
choices.effect: Collaboration skills are just as valuable as the content! Double learning.

choices.label: We'd work together again — we figured it out!
choices.effect: The best teams aren't the ones without disagreements — they're the ones who work through them!

recap_template: You led a group project from planning to presentation! You assigned roles, handled workload issues, mediated disagreements, and delivered as a team.
positive_framing_rules: Never label a team member as lazy or a slacker
Frame disagreements as chances to find better solutions
Celebrate the team process, not just the final product
ai_variation_allowed: Add different types of team challenges

title: Multi-Week Goal
learning_objectives: Adjust plans while keeping the end goal

events.description: Set a 4-week goal! What would you like to accomplish?

choices.label: Run a mile without stopping
choices.effect: Great goal! Week 1: run/walk for 10 minutes. Week 2: run 1/2 mile. Week 3: run 3/4 mile. Week 4: the full mile!

choices.label: Learn 3 songs on guitar
choices.effect: Awesome! Week 1: learn chords. Week 2: first song. Week 3: second song. Week 4: all three!

choices.label: Organize a neighborhood cleanup
choices.effect: Making a difference! Week 1: plan. Week 2: recruit volunteers. Week 3: get supplies. Week 4: cleanup day!

events.description: End of Week 1! You hit your first milestone. But Week 2 brings a challenge: you got sick and missed 3 days. You're behind on your milestone. What do you do?

choices.label: Push milestones back by a few days
choices.effect: Flexible! A few extra days doesn't change the overall goal. Recovery first!

choices.label: Make this week's milestone smaller
choices.effect: A smaller Week 2 milestone is still progress! You can catch up when you feel better.

choices.label: Combine Week 2 and 3 milestones next week
choices.effect: Ambitious catch-up plan! You'll work harder next week but the end date stays the same.

events.description: Week 3. You're back on track! But a friend says 'Why are you even bothering with that?' It stings a little. How do you respond to yourself?

choices.label: I'm doing this for ME, not for them
choices.effect: Your goals don't need anyone else's approval. Internal motivation is the strongest kind!

choices.label: Look at how far you've come — proof it's worth it!
choices.effect: 3 weeks of progress speaks louder than doubt! You can see your own growth.

choices.label: Invite them to join — maybe they'll understand
choices.effect: Your friend tries it and says 'Okay, this is actually cool!' Sometimes people need to see it.

events.description: Week 4 — final week! You're so close to your goal. One last push!

choices.label: Give it everything this week!
choices.effect: You did it! Four weeks of dedication led to an amazing accomplishment!

choices.label: Even if I don't fully finish, I grew so much
choices.effect: The journey IS the achievement! You're so much further than where you started.

choices.label: Finish strong and already plan what's next
choices.effect: Goal achieved and already looking forward! You've built a growth mindset.

recap_template: You set a 4-week goal, created milestones, handled setbacks, and pushed through doubt! Long-term goals teach persistence, flexibility, and self-belief.
positive_framing_rules: Never say the student gave up or let themselves down
Frame setbacks as normal parts of any goal journey
Celebrate effort and growth, not just completion
ai_variation_allowed: Add motivating moments and small wins
